newsitem.title: NEPAL: Five former Nepal ministers rally to PM's side.
newsitem.headline: Five former Nepal ministers rally to PM's side.

text.p: Five former ministers who last month helped spark a political crisis in Nepal by deserting the government said on Monday they had changed their minds and would now support Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba.
The five members of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) were among seven ministers who quit Deuba's government in early December, throwing the Himalayan kingdom into political disarray.
Deuba subsequently narrowly survived a no-confidence motion and he now says that with the help of his RPP partners, he will confirm his majority in parliament.

"It would not be appropriate to push the country towards confusion and instability," the five RPP ministers said in a joint statement on Monday. "There is no alternative but to give continuity to the present government."
Deuba heads a fragile, three-party coalition government linking his centrist Nepali Congress, the RPP and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP).
Nepali Congress has 86 members in the 205-seat House of Representatives, or lower house. The RPP has 19 deputies and the NSP three.
Four RPP renegades had joined the five ministers in deserting Deuba in December, throwing his majority into doubt.
Deuba's 15-month-old coalition survived the no-confidence vote on December 24 when the communist-led opposition fell two votes short of the 103 needed.

But Deuba had only 84 backers in the no-confidence vote, raising doubts about his ability to prove he has a majority and prompting the main opposition United Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, with 87 deputies, to demand Deuba's resignation.

"The present government will prove its majority in parliament for the sake of attaining its goals and moving ahead with determination and self confidence," Deuba said in a statement issued late on Sunday by the state-owned RSS news agency.
Government officials said Deuba planned to prove his majority during the regular winter session of parliament set for February and March. No dates have been set.

RPP officials said unity talks were under way within the party to bring the remaining four dissident members, led by Lokendra Bahadur Chand, leader of RPP's parliamentary delegation, back into the government fold.
By-elections to fill five vacant seats in the lower house, potentially crucial to the government's survival, are set for January 24.
